statusLegend.meaning: Definition or threshold set by design.
Fitted to data by the model code.
Searched so outputs match stated historical targets.
Structural parameter set by judgment; not estimated and not validated on its own.

sections.title: 1 · Data and episode panel
sections.summary: A run-up episode is a market whose real three-year equity return reached +50%. The outcome is what happened over the next four annual closes, which is the same geometry as today (end-2026 to end-2030).

rows.name: Modern equity returns
rows.how: World Bank S&P Global equity indices (CM.MKT.INDX.ZG), deflated by WB consumer-price inflation.

rows.name: Historical equity returns
rows.how: JST total equity return, deflated by JST CPI. Origins before 1994 only, so the two sources never double-count a market.

rows.name: Episode trigger
rows.how: Bubble-scale threshold kept from the original design; origins must be ≥3 years apart within an economy. Run-ups of 100%+ are reported separately.

rows.name: Inflation screen
rows.how: Index returns are not comparable in hyperinflation; removes the affected windows.

rows.name: Outcome window
rows.how: End-2026 origin to end-2030. All probabilities and all paths use this window.

rows.name: Fall bands
rows.how: Worst peak-to-trough fall at annual closes inside the window, measured from the highest close reached since the origin (so an index that rises then falls counts): mild 20–35%, moderate 35–50%, severe 50%+. Measuring from the origin level only, as an earlier release did, lowers the share of falls from 61% to 42%.

rows.name: Boom hurdle
rows.value: 5% a year real (21.6% over four years)
rows.how: A round figure for “keeps earning normal returns”. It splits no-fall cases into boom and contained repricing; no sensitivity run.

rows.name: Panel size
rows.how: Simultaneous crashes make countries non-independent, so intervals resample whole origin years.

rows.name: Predictors
rows.how: Volatility is excluded: an 8-stock basket (NVDA, MSFT, AMZN, AVGO, AMD, ORCL, GOOGL, META) is not comparable with a national index and added no held-out skill.

rows.name: Current state
rows.how: Equal-weight monthly-rebalanced basket to 31 Oct 2026, nominal run-up 217%, deflated by US inflation of 2.8, 2.8, 2.9, 4.1, 8.0% (windows ending Oct 2026 back to Oct 2022). CPI ends in 2024, so the 2025 GDP deflator stands in for 2025–26.

sections.title: 2 · Outcome probabilities: history first, models as a check
sections.summary: The headline weights are what happened after comparable run-ups, with each global wave counted once. Four statistical models were tested against that simple frequency; none held up once whole waves were held out, so they are used for validation, not for the headline.

rows.name: Comparable run-ups
rows.value: 3-year real gain ≥ 100%: 71 episodes in 9 global waves
rows.how: Today's gain is about 190%, inside this group. A global wave is a cluster of origin years within two years of each other; simultaneous crashes count once.

rows.name: Chance of a 20%+ fall
rows.how: Mean over waves of the share of episodes that fell 20%+ peak to trough at annual closes within four years. 10th–90th percentile from a wave bootstrap is shown with each scenario.

rows.name: Split of falls into mild / moderate / severe
rows.how: Taken from the same episodes; with nine waves this split is lumpy, hence the wide ranges.

rows.name: Boom share of no-fall cases
rows.how: Beta(½, ½) Jeffreys prior on the share that clears the real-return hurdle.

rows.name: Model extrapolation (not used)
rows.how: Held out by whole global wave the blend reaches Brier 0.268 against 0.296 for the base rate, but its ranking is no better than chance (AUC 0.44). A recalibration fitted on those held-out predictions has slope -0.19, so the model's extra confidence is not trusted.

rows.name: Ridge logit (run-up + 12-month return)
rows.how: Four-band target, standardised predictors, L-BFGS; penalties chosen a priori.

rows.name: Gradient boosting
rows.how: Shallow and slow to limit overfit; not tuned.

rows.name: Random forest
rows.value: 500 trees · depth 4 · min leaf 5 · max features 0.8 · balanced classes
rows.how: Same reasoning.

rows.name: Blend
rows.how: Set before testing.

rows.name: Folds
rows.how: Whole waves are held out together, because the same global crash seen in many countries is not independent evidence.

rows.name: Sensitivity of the headline
rows.value: fall probability from 72% to 93% across 12 reasonable variants
rows.how: Window length, trigger size, era and predictors all move the number; the full table is in the validation section.

sections.title: 3 · Funding-regime surface
sections.summary: The historical panel cannot see the dollar-liquidity regime today, so a 3 × 3 surface scales the odds of a fall. Its numbers are structural assumptions, not estimates.

rows.name: Geopolitical factor on fall odds
rows.how: Monotone, set by judgment. Applied as a shift in the log-odds of a fall. Rows are percentile bands of the news-based GPR index (calm below 40th, tense 40–80th, crisis above 80th).

rows.name: Liquidity factor on fall odds
rows.how: Monotone, set by judgment. A vacuum means a high-yield spread above 6.5%, reserves below $2.5tn, or equivalent repo and Treasury dysfunction, with two or more signals active (2008 and March 2020 are the analogues).

rows.name: Window-start state weights
rows.value: crisis × neutral 77%; tense × neutral 7%; all nine sum to 100%
rows.how: Carried from the first release’s state model; not re-estimated here.

rows.name: Net effect
rows.how: The surface is the only judgment-set multiplier on the headline; the bootstrap perturbs it by a lognormal factor (sd 0.16).

sections.title: 4 · From equity loss to banking crisis
sections.summary: How a 50%+ fall splits into liquidity holds / vacuum / banking crisis. A second logit, fitted on 150 years of country-years, gives the chance that a banking crisis starts inside the window.

rows.name: Panel
rows.value: 1,924 country-years · 16 economies · origins 1874–2016 · 314 windows with a crisis (16.3%)
rows.how: Every origin year with a consistent real equity record; a crisis counts if JST flags one starting in the window.

rows.name: Features
rows.value: worst 4-year drawdown · 3-year run-up · loans/GDP · 5-year credit change · public debt/GDP · short rate
rows.how: Credit and leverage variables because credit-financed booms end worse.

rows.name: Model
rows.value: ridge logit, C = 0.2, median imputation, standardised
rows.how: Penalty chosen a priori.

rows.name: Held-out skill (Brier vs base rate)
rows.how: Beats the base rate on held-out economies (AUC 0.67) but not on held-out eras (AUC 0.57). The systemic share is therefore wide: the bootstrap draws it from Beta(16·s + ½, 16·(1−s) + ½).

rows.name: Current balance-sheet curve
rows.how: Latest JST US row for credit variables (vintage 2016 origin), overridden by public debt 118.8% of GDP, short rate 4.25% and the current real run-up.

rows.name: Severity integration
rows.value: Gaussian over falls of 50–76%, centre 62%, sd 7.5%
rows.how: Weights the curve over plausible severe falls; gives a systemic share of 34% of severe outcomes.

rows.name: Vacuum without banking crisis
rows.how: No dataset identifies a vacuum that spares the banks; 20% is a central guess, drawn from Beta(2.5, 10.5) in the bootstrap.

sections.title: 5 · Uncertainty and sampling
sections.summary: Every 10th–90th percentile range comes from one bootstrap that resamples whole global waves and perturbs the judgment-set inputs.

rows.name: Bootstrap
rows.value: 500 replications; whole global waves among comparable run-ups resampled with replacement
rows.how: With only 9 waves the ranges are wide on purpose.

rows.name: State weights
rows.how: Concentration set so state weights move by a few points.

rows.name: Regime multiplier
rows.how: Judgment uncertainty in the surface.

rows.name: Boom share, systemic share, vacuum share
rows.value: Beta from resampled counts; Beta(16·s+½, 16·(1−s)+½); Beta(2.5, 10.5)
rows.how: Widths set by judgment.

rows.name: Scenario draws
rows.how: Largest Monte Carlo standard error 0.46%.

rows.name: Not in the bootstrap
rows.how: They are fixed structural parameters; only the macro-damage multipliers (section 7) are randomised. Ranges are therefore narrower than total model uncertainty.

sections.title: 6 · Connected finance engine
sections.summary: One shared state per simulated year, solved by iterating eight times to a fixed point: AI revenue expectations → coverage of commitments → funding cost → equity loss → margin calls → forced sales → liquidity → China outflow → LGFV refinancing → back to liquidity. These coefficients are stress parameters set so each loop behaves as the cited mechanisms describe. They are not estimated.
equations: expectations_t = clip(1 − sev · shape_t + ε_t, 0.03, 1.12),  shape = [0, .95, .82, .58, .38],  ε ~ N(0, 0.07)
revenue = clip(0.70 + 0.40·expectations − 0.15·liquidity, 0.12, 1.15);  commitments = 1 + 0.48·sev·e^(−0.18(t−1))
coverage = 1.82 · revenue / commitments
margin_t = 0.36·margin_{t−1} + max(0, drawdown_t − drawdown_{t−1} − 0.025) · (1.18 + 0.72·sev)
outflow = clip(0.08 + 0.50·liq + 0.34·(1 − expectations) + 0.25·chinaStress, 0, 1)
sale = clip(0.025 + 0.40·max(0, outflow − 0.30) + 0.18·chinaStress, 0, 0.72)
liquidity_t = clip(0.44·liquidity_{t−1} + 0.76·max(0, 1 − coverage) + 1.12·margin + 0.34·sale − policy, 0, 1);  policy = 0.075·(t−1)·sev·(1 − 0.55·margin)
equity_t = clip(0.54·equity_prev + 0.46·100·(1 − 0.52·sev·shape − 0.20·liquidity − 0.10·margin) + N(0, 1.45), 10, 150)
chinaStress_t = clip(0.58·chinaStress_{t−1} + 0.35·outflow + 0.24·liquidity + 0.11·sev, 0, 1);  start 0.22
hyperscaler rate = 4.8 + 5.2·liquidity + 1.3·max(0, 1 − coverage);  LGFV rate = 4.5 + 5.1·outflow + 1.35·sale

rows.name: Boom holds
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 4%; target band under 20%.

rows.name: Contained repricing
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 12%; target band under 20%.

rows.name: Mild adjustment
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 28%; target band 20–35%.

rows.name: Moderate burst
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 50%; target band 35–50%.

rows.name: Deep drawdown, liquidity holds
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 53%; target band 50%+.

rows.name: Severe burst + liquidity vacuum
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 73%; target band 50%+.

rows.name: Severe burst + banking crisis
rows.how: Median simulated annual-close fall 85%; target band 50%+.

rows.name: Funding and margin spirals
rows.how: Equity losses cut collateral, which forces sales and lowers market liquidity.

rows.name: Revenue-expectation reset and sticky commitments
rows.how: Expected AI revenue falls short of what capex and power contracts need; commitments decay slowly.

rows.name: Dollar funding and Treasury channel
rows.how: Outflow from China and dollar scarcity feed back to US liquidity through Treasury sales.

rows.name: LGFV refinancing
rows.how: Marginal refinancing cost for local-government vehicles.

rows.name: Paths
rows.value: 4,000 per scenario; 8 fixed-point iterations per year
rows.how: Common random numbers across scenarios; seed 20261014 + 7 + index.

sections.title: 7 · Macro paths and hysteresis
sections.summary: The finance state drives an output gap and a permanent loss stock. Each of the three US channels (and three China channels) adds to the stock, which decays only slowly. The scales were searched so scenario medians reproduce what happened after equity crashes and banking crises in 1900–2016.
equations: US output gap:  gap_t = (1 − catch)·gap_{t−1} − φ·m·(4.15·liq + 1.85·(1 − exp) + 0.70·margin) + ε,   m ~ lognormal(0, 0.4)
US channels:  C = clip(0.6·liq + 0.4·margin);  I = clip((1.65 − coverage)/1.65);  U = clip(max(0, u − 5)/5)
Hysteresis flow and stock:  flow_t = κ·m'·(0.45·C + 0.30·I + 0.25·U);  scar_t = (1 − ρ)·scar_{t−1} + flow_t
Unemployment:  u_t = 4.3 + okun · max(0, −(gap_t − scar_{t−1}))
Growth:  g_t = 2.4 + (gap_t − gap_{t−1}) − flow_t;   output vs trend = gap − scar
China channels:  D = clip((LGFV rate − nominal growth − 2)/8);  B = clip((chinaStress − 0.30)/0.5);  F = clip((outflow − 0.30)/0.5);  flow = κ_cn·m'·(0.40·D + 0.35·B + 0.25·F)
China output gap uses 2.85·max(0, chinaStress − 0.22) + 1.85·max(0, outflow − 0.135) + 0.45·max(0, sale − 0.065); deflator = −0.92 − 1.5·max(0, chinaStress − 0.22)
Europe: same structure at half the hysteresis scale (credit and labour channels only); Switzerland scales the US path by 0.48.

rows.name: φ, US cyclical scale
rows.how: Grid search (0.30–1.20) minimising squared distance to the 2030 shortfall and trough targets below.

rows.name: κ, US hysteresis scale
rows.how: Grid search (0–5.0) jointly with φ and catch-up; pinned by the persistence target.

rows.name: catch, US output-gap closure
rows.how: Searched over {0.20, 0.30}; a rebound penalty stops growth exceeding 1.9% after 2028 because history shows no catch-up above trend.

rows.name: ρ, decay of the permanent stock
rows.how: 3% a year: slow enough that most of the loss survives a decade.

rows.name: Okun coefficient
rows.how: Literature range about 0.4–0.6 unemployment points per point of output gap.

rows.name: Macro-damage multipliers
rows.value: lognormal sd 0.40 on φ and κ (US and China, separate draws)
rows.how: Widens bands toward the historical spread; check below.

rows.name: Channel weights
rows.how: Credit allocation weighs most because the post-crisis evidence points to impaired intermediation; not separately identified.

rows.name: φ_cn, κ_cn, catch_cn (China)
rows.how: Fitted on the systemic branch to two anchors: the 2030 shortfall of the banking-crisis class (-8.2%) and Japan’s ten-year shortfall after 1989 (-16.4%). Japan is a single analogue.

rows.name: China baseline growth
rows.value: 4.96% in 2025, then -0.231 points a year to 4.04% in 2030
rows.how: Linear trend of 2012–2025 growth, 2020–22 excluded.

rows.name: Drawdown 35%+ with a banking crisis
rows.value: n 79 · median -8.0% · mean -8.2% · p10 -16.2% · trough median -1.0%
rows.how: Real GDP per head four years after the origin against the ten-year pre-origin trend.

rows.name: Drawdown 20–50%, no banking crisis
rows.value: n 398 · median -2.6% · mean -2.1% · p10 -13.2% · trough median 0.0%
rows.how: Real GDP per head four years after the origin against the ten-year pre-origin trend.

rows.name: Drawdown 10–20%
rows.value: n 287 · median -0.1% · mean 0.1% · p10 -11.0% · trough median 0.0%
rows.how: Real GDP per head four years after the origin against the ten-year pre-origin trend.

rows.name: Drawdown under 10%
rows.value: n 707 · median 0.8% · mean 2.6% · p10 -8.7% · trough median 0.0%
rows.how: Real GDP per head four years after the origin against the ten-year pre-origin trend.

rows.name: Drawdown 50%+, no banking crisis
rows.value: n 39 · median -5.2% · mean -3.5% · p10 -12.9% · trough median 0.0%
rows.how: Real GDP per head four years after the origin against the ten-year pre-origin trend.

A 1960–89 trend is rejected: it extrapolates catch-up growth.

rows.name: IMF adverse-AI scenario
rows.value: global GDP −1.1% and US −1.8% by 2028 vs baseline
rows.how: As reported by Reuters on 13 Oct 2026 (primary chapter not retrieved). Our 2028 US output vs trend: Contained repricing -0.8%, Mild adjustment -2.5%, Moderate burst -5.1%, Severe burst + banking crisis -7.3%. The IMF case sits between our contained and mild branches; ours is a harsher family because it adds forced selling and banking-crisis branches.

rows.name: Europe rebound term
rows.how: A small placeholder for safe-asset inflows and reallocation toward Europe. It is not estimated, and Europe’s possible gains as a safe-asset destination are not otherwise simulated.

sections.title: 8 · Joint US–China crisis
sections.summary: A US banking crisis is the systemic branch of the scenario partition. A China crisis is a latent threshold on each simulated path. Both flags come from the same path, so the overlap is generated, not multiplied.
equations: US flag = scenario is “severe burst + banking crisis”
P(China crisis | path) = logistic(−5.80 + 2.6·max outflow + 1.5·max chinaStress + 0.25·(max LGFV rate − 5) + 0.70·max liquidity + 0.24·low-growth + 1.30·US flag)

Reverse-stress cell (property loss P, spread S): drawdown = clip(0.30 + 0.035·(S − 3) + N(0, 0.055), 0.20, 0.82);  P(US) = logistic(logit(transition(drawdown)) + 0.17·(S − 4));  P(China) = logistic(−3.7 + 0.105·(P − 20) + 0.22·(S − 4) + 1.2·US flag);  Gaussian copula ρ = 0.62;  monotone envelope

rows.name: China-crisis threshold coefficients
rows.how: Structural stress parameters from the first joint-crisis release. No comparable historical China crisis exists, so this layer cannot be validated.

rows.name: Crisis definition (research stage)
rows.value: property decline ≥25%, growth <2%, plus restructuring or recapitalisation stress
rows.how: Motivates the inputs of the threshold above; the simulated flag is the logistic, not a literal test of these conditions. China is currently 22.6% below its 2021 property peak.

rows.name: Copula correlation
rows.how: Strength of the shared shock in the reverse-stress surface; tail dependence beyond a Gaussian copula is not modelled.

rows.name: Intervals
rows.how: Bootstrap of scenario weights multiplied by per-scenario path rates.

rows.name: Selection of stress points
rows.value: grid cells are conditional on a revenue-expectation reset
rows.how: Reported as conditional odds, not as current-trajectory odds.

sections.title: 9 · Validation and known weaknesses
sections.summary: What was tested, what held, and where the work is weak.

rows.name: Frequency check
rows.how: Same window, same definitions, no model.

rows.name: Nearest analogs
rows.how: Model-free comparison with today’s state.

rows.name: Base rate (training frequency)
rows.how: Leave one global wave out; target is a 20%+ peak-to-trough fall.

rows.name: Run-up only (ridge logit)
rows.how: Leave one global wave out; target is a 20%+ peak-to-trough fall.

rows.name: Last-12-month return only (ridge logit)
rows.how: Leave one global wave out; target is a 20%+ peak-to-trough fall.

rows.name: Run-up + return (ridge logit)
rows.how: Leave one global wave out; target is a 20%+ peak-to-trough fall.

rows.name: Full blend (logit + boosting + forest)
rows.how: Leave one global wave out; target is a 20%+ peak-to-trough fall.

rows.name: Out of time
rows.value: Train before 1994, test 1994–2021: blend 0.269 vs base 0.320 · Train 1994–2021, test before 1994: blend 0.378 vs base 0.401
rows.how: Models trained on one era and tested on the other; they beat the base rate there, which is why they are kept for comparison.

rows.name: Reliability by wave
rows.value: said 38% → happened 69% (n 61) · said 46% → happened 73% (n 60) · said 53% → happened 48% (n 60) · said 61% → happened 52% (n 60) · said 73% → happened 62% (n 60)
rows.how: Low predictions came true more often than said, and the top bin less often: the model is over-spread, so its extreme outputs are not used.

rows.name: Parameter sensitivity
rows.value: As released: 91%; Drawdown measured from the origin level (earlier definition): 78%; Run-up trigger +40%: 89%; Run-up trigger +75%: 86%; Run-up trigger +100%: 81%; Boom hurdle 3% a year: 91%; Boom hurdle 7% a year: 91%; Window of 3 annual closes: 72%; Window of 5 annual closes: 92%; Modern era only (1994–2021): 93%; Pre-1994 history only: 76%; Run-up as the only predictor: 80%
rows.how: Core logit before the regime surface, so the first row is the model extrapolation, not the headline.

rows.name: Annual-close resolution
rows.value: US monthly data: 64% of 4-year windows contain a 20% fall; annual closes catch 36%
rows.how: Annual closes miss 44% of the falls monthly data see and understate their depth by a median 8 points, so every fall probability here is conservative. Source: Shiller monthly real S&P 500, 1871–2022 origins.

rows.name: Engine convergence
rows.value: fixed point converged (largest residual 0.0001); multiple equilibria in 0% of paths
rows.how: Same shocks, 40 vs 60 iterations, and starts from liquidity 0 and 1 give the same state.

rows.name: Model risk standard
rows.value: limitations, ranges and challenger models disclosed
rows.how: Practice follows SR 11-7.

rows.name: Few independent crashes
rows.value: 9 global waves behind the headline; about 10 clusters of 50%+ falls
rows.how: Every tail estimate rests on a handful of events.

rows.name: Models do not beat history
rows.how: Why the headline is a frequency, not a model output.

rows.name: Annual time step
rows.how: Margin calls (days) and funding stress (weeks) are collapsed into one fixed point per year. Short, severe liquidity episodes that recover within a year are not resolved. A higher-frequency contagion layer is the main modelling gap.

rows.name: Finance-engine coefficients untested
rows.how: They reproduce the loops qualitatively and land median falls in each band, but are not estimated or bootstrapped.

rows.name: Non-AI shocks
rows.value: energy, bond-yield and fiscal shocks only through the regime surface
rows.how: The scenarios are conditional on an AI reset. A rate or energy shock that also hits AI valuations would be attributed to AI here; the IMF lists those risks separately.

rows.name: Policy response
rows.value: one liquidity-support term; no alternative policy scenarios
rows.how: Central-bank and fiscal responses beyond that term are not simulated.

rows.name: Treasury channel
rows.how: Holdings are attributed by custodian and dealers, the Fed and other buyers can absorb sales; the index is a stress trigger, not a forecast.

rows.name: One China analogue
rows.how: China differs in policy space, capital controls and state-bank structure.

rows.name: Basket is not an index
rows.how: National-index episodes are analogues for a concentrated basket. Attribution of each name’s value to AI is an assumption (see the US section).
